Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Emerson Foster
Member ID: W201693421
Reference Number: POC-9A43271177-74690
Requested Service/CPT: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-16
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-12

To the Cigna Appeals Unit:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-16 (Reference POC-9A43271177-74690). The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with the complete clinical documentation summarized below, to correct that deficiency and request that the determination be reversed.

**1. The determination applied under the plan's coverage policy**

The notice states that this determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. Based on my research, the medical policy that Cigna applies to CPT 27447 is CMM-311: Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty, a musculoskeletal management guideline developed by EviCore for Cigna. That policy states, in a section I was able to obtain: "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of knee replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis." It also defines "Total Knee Replacement" as "a surgical procedure that replaces all compartments of the knee (medial, lateral, and patellofemoral) with prosthetic components."

I want to be transparent that I was not able to obtain the exact, current bullet-point criteria specific to the "Total Knee Replacement Indications" section of this policy (the section that applies directly to CPT 27447), so I am not quoting or attributing any specific total-knee criteria language to the plan. What I can quote, from the same policy document, is the parallel "Partial Knee Replacement Indications" section, which illustrates the categories of evidence this policy generally requires for knee-replacement medical necessity determinations: "Partial knee replacement ... is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met: Imaging or arthroscopic findings show ... severe unicompartmental osteoarthritis ... Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV ... Physical exam demonstrates ... knee stability ... knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) >90º ... Symptoms include ... function-limiting pain at short distances ... for at least three (3) months duration ... loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living ... Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration." I cite this only to show the general categories of evidence (imaging severity, exam findings, functional impairment, and failed conservative care) that this same policy considers relevant to knee-replacement determinations — not as the specific total-knee standard, which I have not been able to obtain and am not quoting.

Because Cigna has not provided me with the specific criteria it found my documentation insufficient to meet, I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, a copy of the exact "Total Knee Replacement Indications" criteria from CMM-311 that were applied to this request, and an itemized statement of which specific criterion or criteria the reviewer found unaddressed by the submitted records.

**2. Documentation addressing medical necessity**

The following clinical information, drawn from the prior authorization packet submitted by Dr. Marchetti, addresses the categories of evidence relevant to a knee-replacement medical necessity review:

- **Duration and nature of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Imaging severity:** Weight-bearing knee radiographs dated 2026-07-21 demonstrate bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, graded Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4.
- **Physical examination findings:** Varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion; range of motion limited to 5–100 degrees (i.e., an arc of motion less than the 90-degree-plus range referenced in the policy's parallel partial-replacement criteria, reflecting significant functional restriction).
- **Functional limitation:** Patient cannot climb stairs without assistance and wakes 3–4 times nightly due to pain, reflecting substantial interference with activities of daily living.
- **Failed conservative/non-surgical management:**
  - Supervised physical therapy (quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion work), 16 weeks, 20 completed visits, 2026-03-29 through 2026-07-19, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
  - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-24, yielding only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Absence of contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker.
- **Treating surgeon:** Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, who has evaluated the patient and recommends total knee replacement.

This record documents, at minimum, radiographic severity (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4, bone-on-bone changes in two compartments), a substantial and objectively documented course of non-surgical management (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection) that has failed to provide durable relief, and significant functional impairment affecting daily activities and sleep. I am enclosing copies of the physical therapy discharge note, the corticosteroid injection record, the 2026-07-21 radiology report, and Dr. Marchetti's clinical notes to support this appeal.

**3. Request**

I ask that Cigna:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27447 based on the enclosed documentation; or
2. If the determination is not reversed, provide the specific "Total Knee Replacement Indications" criteria from CMM-311 that were applied, and identify precisely which criterion or criteria the submitted records do not satisfy, so that any remaining gap can be addressed.

I further request that, because this is a pre-service request for a scheduled surgical procedure, this appeal be processed on an expedited basis to the extent permitted under the plan and applicable South Carolina law, and that I be notified in writing of the outcome.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-12).

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or if additional records are needed.

Sincerely,

Emerson Foster
Member ID: W201693421
